title: SSL Overview Presentation - March 2026
abstract: Official 21-slide overview presentation of the Sustainable Solutions Lab at UMass Boston. Covers vision, mission, leadership team, research publications, collaborative events, Climate Adaptation Forum, current projects (Cape Cod Rail Resilience, C3I Climate Careers, CLIIR, Lumbee Tribe Climate Adaptation, Water Quality in Northeast), and recently completed programs.

Current Projects and Programs

Cape Cod Rail
Resilience
Research
Improve rail safety and climate resilience along the Cape
Main Line by integrating advanced technology with
stakeholder-engaged research methods.
Collaborative effort of MassDOT, UMass Boston, and
AECOM. Innovative approach combining aerial surveys,
hydrological drought analysis, and real-time monitoring
systems at three pilot study sites.

Climate Careers
Curricula
Initiative (C3I)
Funded by the Liberty Mutual Foundation.
Collaborate with industry partners, CBOs, and academic
experts to develop training programs for high-demand blue
and green jobs, providing career pathways for
underrepresented populations, especially low-income
people of color from environmental justice communities.

Collaboration with
Just A Start
• CDC in North Cambridge
• Builds, maintains, and rents out
affordable housing
• YouthBuild workforce development
program
• Pilot solar PV program in 2024
• Collaboration with SSL
• Curriculum development to expand to a
3-month program starting Spring 2026
• Expand employer networking
Photo courtesy of Just A Start

Collaboration with
Just A Start
• CBO in Quincy
• Offers a "Conservation Corps" program
focused on preparing Boston youth for
careers in water management and
conservation.
• Collaboration with SSL
• Curriculum development to provide
training on climate change and resilience,
and overlaps with the wastewater sector
• Two additional days, one in classroom
and one in the field
• Will be integrated into Spring 2026 and
Summer 2026 cohorts
Photo courtesy of X-Cel Education

Community-Led Approach to Climate Adaptation
for the Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina
The Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina (LTNC) has launched a community-led
participatory research and action initiative to address the Tribe’s disaster resilience
needs in collaboration with UMB.
LTN faces:
• Repeated impacts from hurricanes
• Flooding
• Limited access to federal disaster resources.
Initiative will document LTNC’s disaster response experiences.
Funded by UMB Grand Scholarly Challenges Grant.

Recently Completed
Projects and Programs

Climate Inequality &
Integrative Resilience (CLIIR)
Funded by a National Science Foundation Center for Research Innovation in Science,
Environment, and Society (CRISES) planning grant, aimed to understand, through a
transdisciplinary approach, how climate change affects people’s quality of life in unequal ways,
and how those inequalities shape community resilience to climate impacts. The NSF CRISES
program was suspended in 2025.
Thematic Areas
• Climate Migration
• Indigenous Approaches to Resilience
• Climate Change and Health
• Decision Support and the creation of a Decision Support Hub

Improving Water Quality in
the Northeast
Sub-awardee and partner of NEEFC/NEWIN.
Improving access to funding and technical support
for underserved communities addressing water
infrastructure challenges.

Liderazgo project:
Identify eligible Tribes, community empowerment
Tribal entities, and projects + structural analysis, to
across the Northeast. foster leadership among
Latino residents in El Punto,
Lead: Dr. Woods (INENAS) Salem.
Leads: Dr. Sweet (SFE), Dr.
Torres-Ardila (Gastón)

Improving Water Quality in
the Northeast
Liderazgo project: community empowerment + structural
analysis, to foster leadership among Latino residents in El Punto,
Salem.
Young community members are trained as leaders and advocates
for identifying and addressing water-related issues.
Activities included: body mapping, podcasting, writing letters to
reps.
